blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 324 of the Constitution provides for the composition and appointment of the Election Commission of India.
The Election Commission consists of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and such number of other Election Commissioners (ECs) as the President may from time to time fix.
Since October 1993, the Election Commission has functioned continuously as a multi-member body comprising one CEC and two ECs.
The appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners is made by the President of India.
All Commissioners hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
The CEC and other ECs have equal powers, salary, and allowances equivalent to a judge of the Supreme Court.
In case of a difference of opinion among the CEC and other Election Commissioners, the decision is made by majority vote.

The CEC can be removed from office only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court, whereas other ECs can be removed by the President only on the recommendation of the CEC.

blocks.content: Originally, the Election Commission was a single-member body. Since 1989, it has been functioning as a multi-member body. Decisions are taken by majority vote.
